Three years after we graduated, Archer suggested renting a luxury RV.
The five of us would drive to Zion National Park.
He sold it as a belated graduation trip and an engagement celebration.
Before we left, I was the one who planned the route, booked the campsites, and bought all the supplies.
I called four different rental companies before I finally managed to book the RV.
I’d even gone to REI two weeks early to buy warm jackets in everyone’s sizes.
The first night at the campground, we started dividing up the beds.
The RV had two permanent double beds.
Archer, Nico, Bianca, and Chiara quickly claimed them for themselves.
Archer pointed to the narrow bed made from the folded-down dinette table.
“Lyra, there are only four real beds.”
“You’re not picky. You can sleep here.”
Nico grinned.
“If you get cold, I’ll lend you my Patagonia to use as a blanket.”
I swallowed past the knot in my throat and nodded.
I’d been hoping we’d all roast marshmallows by the campfire later.
I carried the trash out to the big campground dumpster.
By the time I got back to our site, the RV was gone.
They had driven off without me, heading to another, more popular campground ten miles away.
